clue.text: Aussie bird, one moving around Baltic capital

indicators.note: the budger is placed round the capital, wrapping it

parts.note: one who budges is a budger, someone who moves
Riga is the capital of Latvia, on the Baltic

explanation.surface: An Australian bird is seen flying around a city on the Baltic coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The budgie is a small parakeet native to Australia, hence an Aussie bird.

clue.text: Girls' drink

definitions.meaning: a collective term for a group of girls
..., also spelt bevvy, is British slang for an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A girls' drink, perhaps something pink at a hen party.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a group, as of girls, and a slang word for a drink.

clue.text: Internal division as shareholders' meeting supports rise for salaried personnel

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting piece sits underneath, so it goes last
in a down clue a rise means reading upwards, so the word for salaried is turned round

parts.note: salaried staff are paid
HR, human resources, is the personnel department
AGM is the annual general meeting of shareholders

explanation.surface: A company row splits the AGM as shareholders back a pay rise for staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise for' turns PAID into DIAP; 'supports' puts AGM below DIAP and HR.
explanation.definitionFit: The diaphragm is the muscular partition dividing chest from abdomen inside the body.

clue.text: Resurrected, become once more dead duck

indicators.note: raised up, so in a down clue the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to die again is to re-die

explanation.surface: A dead duck brought back to life only to die again.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider is a large sea duck prized for its down.

clue.text: In Chinese forecasting system, Tokyo's capital's bound up with yen

indicators.note: the capital letter is held tied inside the name of the Chinese system

parts.note: the I Ching is the ancient Chinese book of divination

indicators.note: a capital is a head letter, so the first letter of Tokyo

explanation.surface: Tokyo's capital markets are bound up with the yen, as told by a Chinese oracle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yen' is not the currency but a longing.
explanation.definitionFit: A yen is a craving or longing, as is an itching for something.

clue.text: Uncovered, got tan, nastily coming up orangey colour

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means the letters read upwards
the outer covering of the words is stripped away, exposing a run of letters within

explanation.surface: Someone sunbathing uncovered got a nasty tan, turning an orange colour.
explanation.walkthrough: The run OTTANNA sits inside 'got tan, nastily'; 'coming up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Annatto is a reddish-orange dye from the seeds of a tropical tree, used to colour cheese.

clue.text: Spill the beans about Blair's leadership and his party

indicators.note: the leading letter of the name

parts.note: Tony Blair led Labour, abbreviated Lab

explanation.surface: Someone tells tales about Tony Blair's leadership and the Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to reveal a secret, an idiom for telling what should be kept quiet.

clue.text: Future leader emerging from exile (1917)

parts.note: the Bolshevik revolutionary came back to Russia from Swiss exile in 1917, soon to head the Soviet state

explanation.surface: A history note: a revolutionary returning from Swiss exile in 1917.
explanation.walkthrough: There is also wordplay the parse cannot show: write the date as nineteen seventeen, and 'emerging from' points to the name sitting across exiLE NINeteen.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bolshevik revolutionary returned to Russia in April 1917 and soon led the Soviet state.

clue.text: Be marched roughly around block at first to sleeping quarters

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the single letter
done roughly, the letters are jumbled
the first letter of the word block

explanation.surface: Someone is marched roughly past a block to their bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' makes BEDCHAMER from BE MARCHED; 'around' puts it round B.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedchamber is an old word for a bedroom, a room for sleeping.

clue.text: This geezer's said to give trouble

definitions.meaning: geezer sounds like geyser, a spring that spouts heated water

explanation.surface: A dodgy geezer is said to be a troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: Geezer is British slang for a man; the clue plays on its sound-alike, the geyser.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in hot water is an idiom for being in trouble or disgrace.

clue.text: Start to diet after rejecting mostly simple, old-fashioned fare

indicators.note: the diet's opening letter comes after the other piece
rejected means thrown back, so the shortened word is turned round
most of the word, losing its final letter

parts.note: a simple person is naive

indicators.note: the first letter of the word diet

explanation.surface: A dieter rejects simple meals in favour of old-fashioned food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts NAIVE to NAIV; 'rejecting' turns that into VIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Viand is an archaic word for an item of food.

clue.text: Made up word incorporating old name, Japanese or Siamese?

indicators.note: the made-up word takes the abbreviations into its body

parts.note: a word that is made up has been coined

explanation.surface: A neologism built from an old name, perhaps Japanese or Siamese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Siamese?' is defined by example: Siamese twins are the conjoined kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Siamese twins are joined at birth, the older term for twins physically joined together.

clue.text: Church painter who supported reform

parts.note: a painter is an artist

explanation.surface: A painter of churches who backed a reform movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartists campaigned in 1830s-40s Britain for electoral reform under the People's Charter.

clue.text: Woman to pull right away

indicators.note: the letter for right is taken away from the word for pull

parts.note: to wrench is to pull hard

explanation.surface: A woman is told to pull the right lever away.
explanation.definitionFit: Wench is an old or jocular word for a girl or young woman.

clue.text: Straightforward arrangement to give information about one like 7

indicators.note: the informer's word goes about the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: to squeal is to inform on someone
A, the indefinite article, means one
7-down was a communist, and a communist is a Red

explanation.surface: A frank deal to inform on a revolutionary like the one at 7.
explanation.definitionFit: A square deal is a fair, honest bargain.

clue.text: Demonstrating terror in capacity of ruler

parts.note: qua is Latin-derived for in the capacity of
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A ruler shows terror while acting in an official role.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaking with fear is how one shows terror, hence trembling.

clue.text: Buying and selling tea with bread around south of India

indicators.note: in a down entry south means below, so the rest sits under the letter

parts.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the bread wraps round the tea

parts.note: nan is Indian flatbread
chai is a word for tea

explanation.surface: A tea trader buys and sells along with bread in southern India.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sees traders as links in a supply sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Buyers and sellers form linked steps of a supply sequence, each passing goods along.

clue.text: Best to choose one parent

parts.note: to opt is to choose
the Roman numeral I is one
Mum is a parent

explanation.surface: Is it best to choose just one parent?
explanation.definitionFit: Optimum means the best or most favourable.

clue.text: I'm not safe to be let loose on programme

indicators.note: the letters are freed to roam into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone protests they are unsafe to be let loose on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'programme' is not a TV show but a political one.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifesto sets out a party's programme of policies.

clue.text: Hand guns to posse? Will the captain wear it?

parts.note: to arm someone is to hand them weapons
a posse is a band of people

explanation.surface: Handing out guns to a posse, with a question about the leader's kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A team captain traditionally wears an armband identifying the role.

clue.text: Go ahead and place your bet, old lady

parts.note: do, used emphatically in a command, urges someone to go ahead
to wager is to place a bet

explanation.surface: A bookie urges an old lady to go ahead and bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager is a widow with a title from her late husband, typically elderly.

clue.text: Greasy ring encircling contents — what's point filling vessel with liquid?

definitions.text: what's point filling vessel with liquid?

indicators.note: the contents of the phrase are letters held within it

explanation.surface: A greasy ring around a pot, and a question about the point of filling it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' is a needle tip, and the vessel may be a vein.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypodermic needle's point draws liquid in or injects it into a vessel such as a vein.

clue.text: Jab somewhere below ribs in celebration

parts.note: the shin is a part of the body well below the ribs
a dig is a jab or poke

explanation.surface: Someone gets poked below the ribs at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is an informal word for a lively party or celebration.

clue.text: Age of revolutionary optimism round start of century

indicators.note: the reversed word goes round the letter
a revolution turns something round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: optimism is hope

indicators.note: the first letter of century

explanation.surface: An age of revolutionary hope at the turn of a century.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns HOPE into EPOH; 'round' puts it about C.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a long period of history, an era.

clue.text: More than one monster draws blood — leading character falls

indicators.note: in a down entry the top letter drops further down the word

parts.note: gores means pierces with horns, drawing blood

explanation.surface: A monster draws blood and the hero falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading character falls' moves the G of GORES down one place.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogres are man-eating giants of folklore, so several monsters.

clue.text: Bitter aristo said to be a dead loss

indicators.note: said out loud, the words give a sound-alike

parts.note: wry can mean bitterly ironic, as in a wry smile; a toff is British slang for an upper-class person

explanation.surface: A bitter aristocrat is said to be a total failure.
explanation.walkthrough: Toff is British slang for an upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beyond saving or repair is a total loss, a dead loss.

clue.text: I've now finished sentence with period — put X against comma initially inserted

indicators.note: the X and the letter are put inside the period

parts.note: an eon is a vast period of time

indicators.note: the X is set against, beside, the next letter
the first letter of the word comma

explanation.surface: A writer finishes a sentence with a full stop, adding X and a comma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sentence' is a prison term, not grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: A former convict says this, having served a prison term.

clue.text: Opening coming with no publicity

indicators.note: the publicity letters are left out of the word for coming

parts.note: advent means arrival or coming
an ad is publicity

explanation.surface: A launch is coming but with no publicity.
explanation.definitionFit: A vent is an opening for air or gas to escape.

clue.text: Intercepted communications stirred up war I urged on both sides

indicators.note: the urged word sits either side of the mixed letters

parts.note: to egg is to urge

indicators.note: stirred, the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A warmonger urged war, stirring things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'urged' alone gives EGGED, as in egged on; the clue's 'on' belongs to 'on both sides', the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To earwig is British slang for eavesdropping, overhearing others' conversations.

clue.text: Slough East social group

parts.note: a snake casts its skin when it sloughs it

explanation.surface: A social class in the east of Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is also a town west of London, not just a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social class, as in the Hindu system.

clue.text: The ultimate footwear model

definitions.meaning: a shoemaker's foot-shaped form on which shoes are made

explanation.surface: The ultimate shoe design.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: final, and the wooden foot used by a cobbler.

clue.text: Press-gang member of Chinese race?

definitions.meaning: read as ..., what a press-gang did to sailors
a long narrow vessel paddled in Chinese festival races

explanation.surface: A press-gang recruit joins a Chinese race.
explanation.walkthrough: Press-gangs forcibly enlisted men into the navy, dragging them aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: forcing aboard ship, split cryptically, and the craft raced at festivals in China.
